input.quote: 6.1 Except as provided in Section 6.2, during the term of this Agreement, the Company shall not participate in any project similar to the Site on the Internet with respect to Deerskin Products or products substantially similar to Deerskin Products (including, without limitation, the products of Wilson's House of Leather, Excelled and companies similar to Wilson's House of Leather and Excelled) and HDI shall have the exclusive right to use of the "Deerskin" brand for a self-contained web site for the offering of Deerskin Products directly to the consumer on the Internet.
input.rationale: Section 6.1 imposes an exclusivity/sole-channel covenant on us as customer: we may not participate in any similar Internet project for Deerskin Products or for "products substantially similar" to them, and HDI holds the exclusive right to the "Deerskin" brand online. This fails the fallback on two material terms. (1) Duration: it runs "during the term of this Agreement", and the term under Section 4.1 auto-renews for successive one-year periods, so the lock-up is open-ended rather than capped at 12 months; our only exit is 90 days' notice, which triggers a Termination Payment under Section 4.2(a) (Net Sales for the preceding 12 months less $800,000, halved). (2) No performance-based release: the Agreement contains no service levels and no termination-for-breach right; the only penalty-free exit (Section 1.6) is a one-off launch-date failure at the outset, after which exclusivity continues regardless of HDI's performance. That is effectively exclusive dealing for the full term with no performance exit. Scope is also broader than a defined product category, extending to competitor-type goods (Wilson's House of Leather, Excelled and similar). The Section 6.2 closeout-merchandise carve-out and HDI's reciprocal covenant in Section 6.3 (which benefits us and we leave untouched) mitigate but do not cure this. Given HDI's build-and-host investment and the reciprocal covenant, we propose the fallback rather than deletion: narrow to Deerskin Products, cap at 12 months from the Effective Date, and release automatically (with no Termination Payment) on HDI's failure to meet its Article 1 delivery and performance obligations.

proposal.summary: Narrow Section 6.1 Company exclusivity to Deerskin Products, 12 months, with automatic performance-based exit
proposal.comment: [Playbook] We cannot accept an exclusivity that binds us to the Deerskin Products channel (and to competitor-like products generally) for the whole rolling term with no performance-based exit, particularly where our only exit carries a Termination Payment. We have narrowed the covenant to Deerskin Products for twelve months from the Effective Date and added automatic release if HDI fails to meet its delivery and performance obligations; HDI's reciprocal exclusivity in Section 6.3 is unchanged.

ops.newText: during the twelve (12) month period commencing on the Effective Date, the Company shall not participate in any project similar to the Site on the Internet with respect to Deerskin Products and HDI shall have the exclusive right to use of the "Deerskin" brand for a self-contained web site for the offering of Deerskin Products directly to the consumer on the Internet. The Company's obligations under this Section 6.1, and HDI's exclusive right hereunder, shall terminate automatically and without penalty (and without any Termination Payment being due) upon HDI's failure to perform any of its material obligations under Article 1, including any failure to meet the dates set forth in Section 1.6, and shall in no event extend beyond such twelve (12) month period.
